<!DOCTYPE html><html><head><title>Git as a Version control Notes</title><link rel="shortcut icon" href="https://ssl.gstatic.com/docs/documents/images/kix-favicon-2023q4.ico"><meta name="referrer" content="origin"><script nonce="JM-hOJolgIPhuQ_IO8BQaA">
        var DOCS_timing = {};
        var DOCS_drawing_load = {};
        var DOCS_drawing_decode = {};

        function _DOCS_record_fn(id) {
          if (window.performance && window.performance.now) {
            DOCS_drawing_load[id] = performance.now();
            const imgEl = document.getElementById(id);
            if (imgEl && imgEl.decode) {
              imgEl.decode().then(() => {
                DOCS_drawing_decode[id] = performance.now();
                if (typeof DOCS_notifyDrawingDecode === 'function') {
                  DOCS_notifyDrawingDecode(id);
                }
              });
            }
          }

          if (typeof DOCS_notifyDrawingLoad === 'function') {
            DOCS_notifyDrawingLoad(id);
          }
        }

        function DOCS_record_drawing_load(id) {
          const imgEl = document.getElementById(id);
          if (imgEl.complete) {
            _DOCS_record_fn(id);
          }
          imgEl.onload = function() {
            _DOCS_record_fn(id);
          }
        }

        document.documentElement.addEventListener(
          'load',
          function(event) {
            if (!event || !event.target) {
              return;
            }
            const target = event.target;

            if (target.tagName == 'IMG' &&  target.id && target.id.startsWith('ed.')) {
              DOCS_record_drawing_load(target.id);
            }
          },
          // Captures load events in the DOM because they do not bubble.
          /* useCapture= */ true
        );

class="c14 doc-content"><h1 class="c20" id="h.kzefng3jkz8n"><span class="c7 c17">Git as a Version control Notes</span></h1><p class="c2"><span class="c1">A version control system (VCS) tracks the history of changes as people and teams collaborate on projects together. -- As developers make changes to the project, any earlier version of the project can be recovered at any time. It gives an insight to which changes were made, by who at what time and as to why they were made.</span></p><p class="c2"><span class="c1">Git is a distributed version control system where every developer has a full copy of the project history unlike the once popular centralized Version control system which needed constant connection to a central repository. Descriptively, Git is a fast, scalable, distributed revision control system with an unusually rich command set that provides both high-level operations and full access to internals.</span></p><p class="c2"><span class="c1">A Repository (Git project) encompasses the entire collection of files and folders associated with a project along with each of the file’s revision history as commits.</span></p><p class="c2"><span>References are a user-friendly representation of hashes used to navigate between versions/commits and objects hence use of the references </span><span class="c7">branches, HEAD, </span><span>and </span><span class="c7">tags.</span><span> A </span><span class="c7">branch</span><span> represents an independent line of development (commit). Branches serve as an abstraction for the edit/stage/commit process, -- </span><span class="c7">also, </span><span>a branch is a pointer to a commit -- the default being the master. The </span><span class="c7">HEAD</span><span> reference tells us which branch we are currently working on while </span><span class="c7">a tag</span><span class="c1"> reference is immutable and is always linked to the same commit to be able to always remember a moment in time.</span></p><p class="c2"><span class="c1">A good practice of using Git is to create a copy of the develop branch and work within the copy while never pushing anything into the production branch directly.</span></p><p class="c2"><span class="c7">Internally,</span><span> Git uses the git</span><span><a class="c4" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://brilliant.org/wiki/secure-hashing-algorithms/%23sha-1&amp;sa=D&amp;source=editors&amp;ust=1751020129930006&amp;usg=AOvVaw32ehIzuNHiOErSgSJlZicS"> </a></span><span class="c19"><a class="c4" href="https://www.google.com/url?q=https://brilliant.org/wiki/secure-hashing-algorithms/%23sha-1&amp;sa=D&amp;source=editors&amp;ust=1751020129930302&amp;usg=AOvVaw0SONhaTBEtbInlepXSGxB6">SHA-1 algorithm</a></span><span> to generate a hashkey of stored values which it uses to identify </span><span class="c7">objects</span><span>. Git generates SHA-1 hash for its three types of objects which are </span><span class="c7">blobs, trees </span><span>and </span><span class="c7">commits </span><span>and persists the contents zipped into the repository. </span><span class="c7">A</span><span> </span><span class="c7">tree</span><span> object in git contains permissions, object type, object hash and filename for each file/subdirectory. The tree points to blobs, or to other trees to create a hierarchical structure. </span><span class="c7">A</span><span> </span><span class="c7">Blob</span><span> is a contraction of “binary large objects” and holds files data but does not contain any metadata about the file or even its name. It represents each version of the file. A blob object is the content of a file and nothing more. </span><span class="c7">A</span><span> </span><span class="c7">commit</span><span class="c1"> points to a tree object that captures in a snapshot of the entire state of the repository at a given point in time.</span></p><p class="c2"><span class="c5">Graphical internal file structure</span><span style="overflow: hidden; display: inline-block; margin: 0.00px 0.00px; border: 0.00px solid #000000; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); width: 624.00px; height: 138.67px;"><img alt="" src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsd/ANYlcfBSfDhPzjjh43QHwa3y7mWyIJkOdNZ5W9Or4mWqo2sWL-4l2FYeaDQqLPf7F-uDS3sfPnZV6ojPWZTetGvdKuO-4QdMpqMWNc1hmh4tmpwjQMTyfqV__7L3yZTj8rrT5bg0hQ1sZ9NwnRRD" style="width: 624.00px; height: 138.67px; margin-left: 0.00px; margin-top: 0.00px; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px);" title=""></span></p><p class="c2"><span class="c1">When dealing with multiple branches, the blob references the common files between the new commit and the parent commit while the tree references the changed files in the new commit.</span></p><p class="c15"><span>                    </span><span class="c5">Graphical internal structure of multiple branches</span><span style="overflow: hidden; display: inline-block; margin: 0.00px 0.00px; border: 0.00px solid #000000; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); width: 624.00px; height: 290.67px;"><img alt="" src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsd/ANYlcfBzxtNWROs-7FdZlSycaxw00CSdyXiHYkfUW18V-0ccTFeKwxgBzt0kCyP3ZHtz5LLA4N9505ui-nzIok5zUF9nN9FUYh9jfVkf0T7iQh17PXjCfw_xCeIRaTD7u9c8sEI3LoTwTwT9z-s3FDM" style="width: 624.00px; height: 290.67px; margin-left: 0.00px; margin-top: 0.00px; transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px); -webkit-transform: rotate(0.00rad) translateZ(0px);" title=""></span></p><p class="c2"><span>To create a new branch locally, switch into the main branch (or the branch you would like to branch from) using </span><span class="c3">git checkout branch-name</span><span class="c16"> </span><span>Enter, and on the next line enter again the command </span><span class="c3">git checkout -b new-branch-name</span><span class="c0">.</span></p><p class="c15"><span>The origin keyword in git is a short representation of the remote URL hence </span><span class="c3">git push origin master </span><span>is equivalent to </span><span class="c3 c9">git push remote-repository-url.git your-branch-name.</span></p><p class="c15"><span class="c1">A pull Request (PR) is a way to alert a repo’s owner that you want to make some changes to their code. It allows them to review the code and make sure it looks good before putting your changes on the primary branch.</span></p><p class="c15"><span class="c7">                    Git rebase: </span><span>this command allows on to easily change a series of commits and modify the history of one’s repositories like reorder, edit and squash commits together, </span><span class="c7">However, </span><span class="c1">it is considered bad practice to rebase commits after pushing to a repository because it complicates work for everyone else using the repository. Examples:</span></p><p class="c12"><span>1.</span><span class="c8">       </span><span class="c16">git rebase –interactive other-branch-name </span><span class="c1">:This command rebases all the commits between other-branch-name and the current branch.</span></p><p class="c12"><span>2.</span><span class="c8">       </span><span class="c16">git rebase –interactive  HEAD~7</span><span class="c1">  :This command allows you to rebase the last few commits in your current branch.</span></p><p class="c6"><span class="c1">These two commands open an interactive text editor like terminal.</span></p><p class="c13"><span class="c10">While rebasing, six command are available which are:</span></p><p class="c6"><span>1.</span><span class="c8">       </span><span class="c0">pick : This includes a commit and its arrangement’s order during  rebasing changes the order of the commits. Non-included commit lines should be deleted.</span></p><p class="c6"><span>2.</span><span class="c8">       </span><span class="c0"> reword : With similarity to pick, here one is given a chance to change the commit message with changes made not affecting the commit.</span></p><p class="c6"><span>3.</span><span class="c8">       </span><span class="c0">edit : This provides more options to the commit than reword like amending (add or change) commits, make more commits, split larger commits to small ones and remove erroneous changes made in a commit.</span></p><p class="c6"><span>4.</span><span class="c8">       </span><span class="c0">squash :This allows you to combine two or more commits into a single commit which is above it  in a form of merging giving a chance to name a new commit message.</span></p><p class="c6"><span>5.</span><span class="c8">       </span><span class="c0">fixup :Similar to squash, the commit message  used is of the one above it while the one to be merged ‘s is discarded.</span></p><p class="c6"><span>6.</span><span class="c8">       </span><span class="c0">exec :This lets you  run arbitrary shell commands against a commit.</span></p><p class="c15"><span class="c1"> </span></p><p class="c18"><span class="c1"></span></p></div></div><script nonce="JM-hOJolgIPhuQ_IO8BQaA">function _F_toggles_initialize(a){(typeof globalThis!=="undefined"?globalThis:typeof self!=="undefined"?self:this)._F_toggles=a||[]}_F_toggles_initialize([]);
